lesson.title: Multi-Step Reasoning
lesson.summary: Teach reviewers to reason in ordered steps: observation, hypothesis, supporting evidence, contradicting evidence, alternative interpretation, risk assessment, article selection, rejection, confidence adjustment, and final recommendation.
learningObjectives: Start with observation before forming a hypothesis.
Compare supporting evidence against contradicting evidence.
Test alternative interpretations before finalizing a recommendation.
Explain why a stronger explanation won over weaker alternatives.
Adjust confidence explicitly after each reasoning step.
Separate applicable GCAM articles from rejected articles.

concepts.title: Evidence Collection
concepts.summary: Collect the facts needed before forming a hypothesis.

concepts.title: Multi Evidence Reasoning
concepts.summary: Compare multiple pieces of evidence and decide which interpretation is best supported.

concepts.title: Contradiction Resolution
concepts.summary: Resolve supporting and contradicting evidence before finalizing the answer.

concepts.title: Confidence Assessment
concepts.summary: Adjust confidence after weighing support, contradiction, and alternative explanations.

concepts.title: Finding Generation
concepts.summary: Turn the reasoned conclusion into a reviewer finding when the evidence is strong enough.

concepts.title: Report Priority
concepts.summary: Choose the final recommendation and keep the report aligned to the best explanation.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Begin with the literal observation before any hypothesis is formed.
evidenceRequirements: State the observed fact in the scene.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Propose the best supported explanation without skipping alternatives.
evidenceRequirements: Name the hypothesis and the evidence behind it.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: What evidence supports or contradicts it?
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Compare supporting evidence against contradicting evidence explicitly.
evidenceRequirements: List at least one supporting clue and one contradicting clue when present.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Test alternate readings before committing to the final answer.
evidenceRequirements: Describe the alternative interpretation and why it is weaker or stronger.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Assess risk, ambiguity, and whether the evidence is still borderline.
evidenceRequirements: State the remaining uncertainty or risk.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Select the final recommendation only after confidence is adjusted.
evidenceRequirements: State the final recommendation and confidence adjustment.

examples: The reviewer observes a line, tests a counterfactual explanation, and only then finalizes the conclusion.
Supporting evidence survives contradiction checks and becomes the best explanation.
An alternative interpretation is considered and rejected because the stronger reading is better supported.
Confidence drops after contradictory evidence appears, even though the first clue looked strong.
counterExamples: The reviewer jumps from observation directly to conclusion without testing alternatives.
The reviewer ignores contradicting evidence because it appears later.
The reviewer treats the first plausible explanation as the best one.
The reviewer adjusts confidence without explaining why the evidence changed.

minimum: Compare at least one supporting explanation against at least one alternative when available.
strong: The hypothesis is supported by multiple aligned clues.
Contradicting evidence has been checked and answered.
weak: The hypothesis is plausible but still depends on missing context.
The evidence supports the idea only weakly.
insufficient: The reviewer cannot explain why the chosen interpretation wins.
The explanation skips directly from observation to recommendation.
confidenceGuidance: High confidence when the best explanation survives counterfactual testing.
Medium confidence when the strongest reading is supported but not fully closed.
Low confidence when contradiction or ambiguity remains.
Review required when no explanation clearly beats the alternatives.

conceptRelationships.note: Observed evidence feeds the comparison stage.
The reviewer compares supporting and contradicting evidence.
Confidence changes after contradiction is resolved.
The final recommendation depends on the confidence level.
The report prioritizes the final recommendation and rejected alternatives.

glossaryReferences.note: Alternative interpretations are compared before the final conclusion.
The best explanation is the one that survives comparison.
Confidence should change after the evidence is weighed.

gcamMappings.note: The reasoning begins with an observation.
Supporting and contradicting evidence are compared.
The final recommendation follows the confidence update.

reportTemplates.reasonTemplate: Observation: {{observation}}. Hypothesis: {{hypothesis}}. Supporting evidence: {{supportingEvidence}}. Contradicting evidence: {{contradictingEvidence}}. Alternative interpretation: {{alternativeInterpretation}}. Confidence: {{confidence}}.
reportTemplates.recommendationTemplate: Explain why the best explanation won, which articles were applicable, which were rejected, and how confidence changed.

metadata.subject: reviewer methodology
decisionRules: do not jump from observation to conclusion
decisionExamples: The reviewer explains why the direct interpretation wins over the counterfactual reading.
The reviewer lowers confidence after contradictory evidence appears.
decisionExceptions: Quotation can preserve the observation while lowering confidence.
Historical framing can change the risk assessment.
Dream or flashback context can shift the final recommendation.
